content.text: Modern Andhra under Company Rule: Northern Circars & Sir Arthur Cotton

The British colonization of Andhra unfolded in stages: the acquisition of the Northern Circars from the Nizam in 1765–1768, followed by the acquisition of the Ceded Districts (Rayalaseema) in 1800. Plagued by ruthless revenue extortion and devastating famines (notably the Guntur Famine of 1832), the coastal Andhra delta was rescued from economic ruin by the visionary hydraulic engineering of Sir Arthur Cotton, whose anicuts on the Godavari and Krishna transformed coastal Andhra into the granary of South India.

content.caption: The Dowleswaram Barrage on the Godavari River near Rajahmundry, engineered by Sir Arthur Cotton in 1852.
Colonial Administrative & Hydraulic Milestones in Modern Andhra
rows: Coastal Andhra (Srikakulam to Guntur); Robert Clive & Nizam Ali Khan.
Clive secured imperial Farman from Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II (1765); confirmed by 1768 treaty with Nizam; Guntur Circar ceded in 1788.
Imposed Permanent Zamindari Settlement in coastal estates (Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Nuzvid, Pithapuram); triggered severe agrarian distress.
Rayalaseema (Bellary, Anantapur, Cuddapah, Kurnool); Lord Wellesley & Nizam.
Ceded by Nizam to Company to pay for British subsidiary force; placed under Principal Collector Major Thomas Munro (1800–1807).
Munro pacified turbulent Poligars (feudal palegars); surveyed 10 million acres; introduced the Ryotwari settlement directly with cultivators, earning the affectionate title 'Munro Sahib'.
Total failure of monsoon exacerbated by ruthless revenue extraction and lack of irrigation; one-third of Guntur's population (150,000 people) perished.
Devastated agriculture, depopulated fertile villages, and exposed the lethal vulnerability of rain-dependent coastal deltas.
Godavari Anicut at Dowleswaram (1852) & Krishna Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada (1855).
Engineered 4-kilometer masonry weir across 4 arms of the Godavari at Dowleswaram; built Krishna anicut at Vijayawada with vast canal irrigation and navigation networks.

Brought over 2 million acres under assured double-crop irrigation; eradicated famine in the deltas; transformed East and West Godavari into the 'Rice Bowl of India'; Cotton revered as 'Apara Bhagiratha'.

items: Thomas Munro's Legacy: Respected local traditions; granted tax remissions during bad harvests; allocated revenues to the Tirumala temple; revered in Rayalaseema folklore as 'Mandava Rishi' and 'Munro Sahib'.

Sir Arthur Cotton ('Delta Cotton'): British military engineer who argued that water, not railways, was the true wealth of India; overcame severe bureaucratic resistance from the Court of Directors to complete the Dowleswaram Anicut in 1852; grateful Telugu farmers still perform 'Cotton Tarpanam' during Godavari Pushkarams.

Resistance of Poligars: Fierce armed resistance against British tax collection led by Rayalaseema Poligars, most notably Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy (Kurnool, 1846), who attacked colonial treasuries before being captured and hanged publicly at Koilkuntla on 22 February 1847.
Commercialization & Ports: Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, and Machilipatnam developed as ports for rice, tobacco, and cotton exports; growth of local printing presses and urban intelligentsia.

content.text: Part A: Mains Analytical & Descriptive Questions

items:
Critically evaluate the colonial acquisition of coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema, and assess the transformative impact of Sir Arthur Cotton's hydraulic projects on the agrarian economy of Andhra Pradesh. (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Detail the political annexation: Northern Circars via Clive's Farman (1765/1768) and Ceded Districts via Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance (1800); analyze the socio-economic devastation of Company rule: Munro's high initial Ryotwari assessments and the catastrophic Guntur Famine of 1832 (Nandana Karuvu); evaluate Sir Arthur Cotton's hydraulic genius: constructing the Dowleswaram Anicut across the Godavari (1852) and Krishna anicut at Vijayawada (1855); explain how 2 million acres of drought-prone wasteland transformed into fertile double-cropped paddy deltas, sparking the economic surplus that later funded the 19th-century Andhra cultural renaissance.

content.text: Part B: Screening / Prelims Objective Questions

items:
Q1. Which British hydraulic engineer, celebrated across Andhra as 'Apara Bhagiratha', designed and constructed the historic Dowleswaram Anicut across the Godavari River in 1852?
(a) Sir Thomas Munro
(b) Sir Arthur Cotton
(c) Colonel Colin Mackenzie
(d) Sir Alexander Read
Correct Answer: (b) Sir Arthur Cotton [Explanation: General Sir Arthur Cotton designed the landmark Dowleswaram Anicut (1847–1852) on the Godavari and the Krishna Barrage (1855), permanently banishing famines from the deltas.]

Q2. The catastrophic 'Guntur Famine' of 1832, which wiped out over a third of the population of Guntur district, is traditionally remembered in Telugu folklore as:
(a) Dhatubadi Karuvu
(b) Nandana Karuvu
(c) Pedda Karuvu
(d) Rayalaseema Karuvu
Correct Answer: (b) Nandana Karuvu [Explanation: The Guntur Famine occurred in the Telugu cyclical year 'Nandana' (1832 CE) and is famously commemorated as 'Nandana Karuvu', which decimated the Krishna-Godavari region.]

Q3. The four districts of Rayalaseema (Bellary, Anantapur, Cuddapah, Kurnool) acquired by the British from the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1800 were historically termed:
(a) Northern Circars
(b) Ceded Districts (Datta Mandalamulu)
(c) Agency Tracts
(d) Carnatic Territories
Correct Answer: (b) Ceded Districts (Datta Mandalamulu) [Explanation: In 1800, Nizam Ali Khan ceded these territories to the British to finance the Subsidiary force, earning them the title 'Ceded Districts' until renamed 'Rayalaseema' in 1928.]

Q4. Which brave Rayalaseema Poligar led an armed rebellion against British East India Company oppression in 1846 and was publicly hanged at Koilkuntla in 1847?
(a) Alluri Sitarama Raju
(b) Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy
(c) Veerapandiya Kattabomman
(d) Marthanda Varma
Correct Answer: (b) Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy [Explanation: Polygar Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy of Kurnool rebelled in 1846, raiding British treasuries; he was captured and hanged in February 1847, a decade before 1857.]

Q5. Who was appointed as the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800, successfully pacifying the Poligars and introducing the Ryotwari settlement?
(a) Sir Arthur Cotton
(b) Major Thomas Munro
(c) Lord Wellesley
(d) Robert Clive
Correct Answer: (b) Major Thomas Munro [Explanation: Major (later Sir) Thomas Munro served as Principal Collector from 1800 to 1807, implementing fair Ryotwari assessments and winning the affection of the Rayalaseema peasantry.]
